# smphe — Semaphore UI CLI

CLI for [Semaphore UI](https://semaphoreui.com/), an open-source web UI for running Ansible, Terraform, Bash, and Python automation tasks.

Package: `@gzl10/semaphore-client`
Install: `npm install -g @gzl10/semaphore-client`

## Setup

```bash
smphe config set host http://semaphore.example.com:3000
echo "$YOUR_API_TOKEN" | smphe login --token-stdin   # never --token: argv lands in history and `ps`
smphe use <projectId>   # set active project for all subsequent commands
```

## Configuration

Precedence is **flags → environment → config file**, per clig.dev.

| Setting | Resolution order |
|---|---|
| Host | `SMPHE_HOST` → config file |
| Token | `SMPHE_TOKEN_FILE` (a path) → `SMPHE_TOKEN` → config file |
| Project | `--project <id>` → `SMPHE_PROJECT` → `smphe use <id>` |

Config file: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/smphe/config.json` (i.e. `~/.config/smphe/config.json`), directory
`700`, file `600`. An older `~/.smphe-client/config.json` keeps being used if it exists; nothing is
moved automatically.

**Do not put the token in `SMPHE_TOKEN` if you can avoid it**: environment variables are inherited by
child processes, appear in `docker inspect` and in systemd unit state, and reach crash dumps. Use
`SMPHE_TOKEN_FILE=/run/secrets/smphe` in CI and containers.

`smphe config show` prints where each value comes from, e.g. `host: http://… (from SMPHE_HOST)`, so a
forgotten `export` cannot redirect commands silently.

## JSON output

All read commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output:

```bash
smphe tasks list --json | jq '.[].status'
smphe templates list --json | jq '.[] | {id, name, playbook}'
```

## Commands

### Setup
```
smphe config set host <url>      Set Semaphore host URL
smphe config set token <token>   Set API token (discouraged: argv is visible to other processes)
smphe config show                Show current config, and where each value comes from
smphe login --token-stdin        Read the token from stdin — the way to do it
smphe login --token <token>      Same, but leaves the token in your shell history and in `ps`
smphe use <projectId>            Set active project
```

### Projects
```
smphe projects list
smphe projects get <id>
smphe projects create --name <name>
smphe projects update <id> --name <name>
smphe projects delete <id>
```

### Templates (playbooks / runbooks)
```
smphe templates list
smphe templates get <id>
smphe templates create --name <name> --inventory-id <id> --repository-id <id> --environment-id <id> --playbook <file.yml>
                       [--environment-ids <id,id>] [--app <app>] [--git-branch <branch>]
smphe templates update <id> [--name <name>] [--playbook <file>] [--app ansible|terraform|tofu|bash|python|powershell]
smphe templates delete <id>
```

### Tasks (executions)
```
smphe tasks list [--status waiting|starting|waiting_confirmation|confirmed|rejected|running|stopping|stopped|error|success]
smphe tasks get <taskId>
smphe tasks run <templateId> [--limit <hosts>] [--debug] [--dry-run] [--playbook <file>] [--environment <json>] [--arguments '["--tags","deploy"]']
smphe tasks stop <taskId>
smphe tasks output <taskId>
```

`tasks run` returns immediately with `status: "waiting"`. Poll with `tasks get` until `success`, `error` or
`stopped` — the only final statuses. A task behind a workflow approval gate sits in `waiting_confirmation`,
and a denied one stays `rejected` forever.

### Keys (credentials / SSH keys)
```
smphe keys list
smphe keys get <id>
smphe keys create --name <name> --type none|ssh|login_password|string
                  [--private-key <content>] [--private-key-file <path>] [--login <user>] [--password <pass>] [--string <value>]
smphe keys update <id> [--name <name>] [--type none|ssh|login_password|string] [--private-key <content>] [--private-key-file <path>] [--login <user>] [--password <pass>] [--string <value>]
smphe keys delete <id>
```

### Inventory (host lists)
```
smphe inventory list
smphe inventory get <id>
smphe inventory create --name <name> --inventory <content> --type static|file|static-yaml|terraform-workspace|tofu-workspace|terragrunt-workspace [--ssh-key-id <id>]
smphe inventory update <id> [--name <name>] [--inventory <content>] [--type <type>] [--ssh-key-id <id>]
smphe inventory delete <id>
```

`--ssh-key-id` is optional: a static inventory works without a key (the API
returns `ssh_key_id: null`). Give it only when the inventory needs credentials.

### Environment (variable groups / secrets)
```
smphe environment list
smphe environment get <id>
smphe environment create --name <name> [--password <vault-key>]
                         [--var KEY=VALUE...] [--extra-var KEY=VALUE...]
                         [--secret-var KEY=VALUE...] [--secret-env KEY=VALUE...] [--from-env <path>]
smphe environment update <id> [--name <name>] [--var KEY=VALUE...] [--extra-var KEY=VALUE...]
                              [--secret-var KEY=VALUE...] [--secret-env KEY=VALUE...] [--delete-secret <name>...]
                              [--password <vault-key>]
smphe environment delete <id>
```

`--password` is the ansible-vault encryption key for the variable group, not an auth password.

### Repositories
```
smphe repositories list
smphe repositories get <id>
smphe repositories create --name <name> --git-url <url> --git-branch <branch> --ssh-key-id <id>
smphe repositories update <id> [--name <name>] [--git-url <url>] [--git-branch <branch>] [--ssh-key-id <id>]
smphe repositories delete <id>
```

### Schedules
```
smphe schedules list
smphe schedules get <id>
smphe schedules create --template-id <id> --cron "0 2 * * *" [--name <name>]
smphe schedules update <id> [--cron <format>] [--name <name>] [--template-id <id>] [--enabled] [--no-enabled]
smphe schedules delete <id>
```

`--no-enabled` pauses a schedule without deleting it. `--enabled` reactivates it.

### Workflows (chains of templates, Semaphore >= 2.19)
```
smphe workflows list
smphe workflows get <id>
smphe workflows create --file <graph.json> [--name <name>]
smphe workflows update <id> [--file <graph.json>] [--name <name>]
smphe workflows delete <id>
smphe workflows run <id>
smphe workflows runs <id>
smphe workflows stop <id> <runId>
smphe workflows approvals <id> <runId>
smphe workflows approve <id> <runId> <nodeId>
smphe workflows reject <id> <runId> <nodeId>
```

A workflow is a graph of task templates that runs as one unit, with optional
approval gates. Graph file format:

```json
{
  "name": "deploy-with-approval",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": 1, "kind": "task", "templateId": 5 },
    { "id": 2, "kind": "approval", "approvalMessage": "Ship it?" },
    { "id": 3, "kind": "task", "templateId": 8 }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "sourceNodeId": 1, "destinationNodeId": 2, "condition": "on_success" },
    { "sourceNodeId": 2, "destinationNodeId": 3, "condition": "on_success" }
  ]
}
```

Node `kind`: `task` (needs `templateId`), `approval` (gate; optional
`approvalMessage` and `approvalTimeout`) or `note` (annotation).
Edge `condition`: `on_success`, `on_failure` or `always`.

Gotchas:
- Node `id` is client-side and only wires the edges — the server assigns the
  real ids. It is REQUIRED as soon as the graph has edges, or the API answers
  `workflow edge source node does not belong to workflow`.
- The graph needs exactly one root node (a node no edge points to).
- `run` returns `root_task_id`: follow it with `smphe tasks output <id>`.
- A run stops at an approval gate with status `approval`; list the pending
  gates with `workflows approvals` and resolve them with `approve`/`reject`.
- These endpoints answer on any 2.19 server, but a build with the feature
  disabled serves a stub: `list` returns an empty table and the rest 404.

### Integrations (webhooks that run a template)
```
smphe integrations list
smphe integrations get <id>
smphe integrations create --name <n> --template-id <id> [--auth-method <m>] [--auth-secret-id <id>] [--auth-header <h>] [--searchable]
smphe integrations update <id> [--name <n>] [--template-id <id>] [--auth-method <m>] [--auth-secret-id <id>] [--auth-header <h>] [--searchable] [--no-searchable]
smphe integrations delete <id>

smphe integrations matchers list <integrationId>
smphe integrations matchers get <integrationId> <matcherId>
smphe integrations matchers create <integrationId> --name <n> --match-type <header|body> --method <equals|unequals|contains> --key <k> --value <v> [--body-data-type <json|string>]
smphe integrations matchers update <integrationId> <matcherId> [...]
smphe integrations matchers delete <integrationId> <matcherId>
smphe integrations matchers refs <integrationId> <matcherId>

smphe integrations values list <integrationId>
smphe integrations values get <integrationId> <valueId>
smphe integrations values create <integrationId> --name <n> --value-source <body|header> --variable <VAR> [--variable-type <environment|task>] [--key <k>] [--body-data-type <json|string>]
smphe integrations values update <integrationId> <valueId> [...]
smphe integrations values delete <integrationId> <valueId>
smphe integrations values refs <integrationId> <valueId>

smphe integrations aliases list [--integration <id>]
smphe integrations aliases create [--integration <id>]
smphe integrations aliases delete <aliasId> [--integration <id>]
```

An external `POST /api/integrations/{alias}` runs the integration's template.
Matchers decide which requests count; extract values copy parts of the request
into the task (`--variable-type environment` for an env var, `task` for a task
param).

Gotchas (verified on 2.19.8):
- `searchable` decides which alias works, and only one of the two does.
  `false`: only its own alias fires it, and its matchers are NEVER evaluated.
  `true`: its own alias stops answering, and it is reached only through the
  project-wide alias (`aliases create` with no `--integration`), which picks it
  by matchers — one with no matchers never fires.
- The alias string cannot be chosen: the server generates a random one and
  returns `{id, url}`. This client adds `alias`, taken from the last segment of
  `url`. `url` is built from the server's `web_host`, so it can point at
  `localhost` while the alias itself is correct.
- The webhook answers `204` whether it ran something, failed authentication or
  matched nothing. The only proof a task started is the response header
  `X-Semaphore-Task-ID`.
- Every auth method other than `none` reads its secret from a project key
  (`--auth-secret-id`); `token` and `hmac` also need `--auth-header`.
- PUT is full-replace, as everywhere: `update` reads and merges first. A
  hand-made partial body answers 400 without `template_id`, and with it answers
  204 after silently clearing the auth fields.
- Deleting an integration removes its own aliases; a project-wide alias
  survives and has to be deleted on its own.
- `GET /integrations/{id}/refs` is a stub on the server (always
  `{matchers: null, values: null}`), so there is no CLI command for it.

### Admin surface (apps, global roles, instance task pool)
```
smphe apps list [--all]
smphe apps get <appId>
smphe apps set <appId> [--title <t>] [--icon <i>] [--color <c>] [--dark-color <c>] [--path <p>] [--priority <n>] [--active] [--no-active]
smphe apps enable <appId>
smphe apps disable <appId>
smphe apps delete <appId>

smphe roles list
smphe roles get <slug>
smphe roles create <slug> --name <name> [--permissions <bitmask>]
smphe roles update <slug> [--name <name>] [--permissions <bitmask>]
smphe roles delete <slug>

smphe instance tasks [--queued] [--running]
smphe instance stop <taskId>
```

All of it needs a GLOBAL ADMIN token: a non-admin gets 403 with an empty body.

Gotchas (verified on 2.19.12):
- `apps set` on an unknown id CREATES the app: the server does not validate it.
  But the id becomes part of an option key validated against `^[\w.]+$`, so a
  hyphen is rejected — and since the server writes one option per field and
  stops at the first bad key, it answers 500 with some fields already written,
  a different subset each time. The CLI refuses such ids before sending.
- The PUTs are full replaces, as everywhere: a partial body leaves an app
  `active:false priority:0` and a role `permissions:0`. `set`/`update` merge.
- `instance tasks` is NOT task history: it is the in-memory pool, only what is
  queued or running, with `location` saying which. `location` is not `status`:
  a task reads `location:running` while its `status` is still `waiting`.
- `instance stop` does not delete: it stops the task, and the server answers 204
  whether or not the task was in the pool. The CLI says which of the two it was.
- Global roles work on the OSS image even though the controller comes from the
  PRO package and `custom_roles_management` reports false. Runners and the
  Terraform backend really are PRO and are not covered.

### Backup (whole-project export/import)
```
smphe backup export [--file <path>]
smphe backup restore --file <path>
```

Semaphore has no config-as-code (upstream issue #3109), so this is the closest
thing to keeping a project under version control. `export` without `--file`
prints JSON to stdout; with `--file` it writes it with mode 600.

`restore` always creates a NEW project, it never overwrites an existing one.
Secrets are not exported in plain text: a restored project needs its keys and
secret values set again.

### Users
```
smphe users list
smphe users get <id>
```

## Typical agent workflow

```bash
# 1. Discover what playbooks are available
smphe templates list --json

# 2. Run a playbook
smphe tasks run 42 --limit webservers --json
# → {"id": 123, "status": "waiting", ...}

# 3. Poll until done
smphe tasks get 123 --json | jq '.status'
# → "running" ... "success"

# 4. Get output on failure
smphe tasks output 123

# 5. Pause a schedule temporarily
smphe schedules update 7 --no-enabled

# 6. Re-enable it
smphe schedules update 7 --enabled
```
